title: Ephemeral scratch stride allocator and KV lazy materialization to trim transient GPU workspace
author: Rohan Patel
release_notes: Introduces an ephemeral stride-based scratch allocator and a lazy-KV materialization path that reduce peak transient GPU memory by up to 28% on long-sequence workloads. No public API changes. Runtime flag: --enable-ephemeral-scratch (experimental).
description: Motivation: long-sequence, multi-stream workloads showed repeated transient workspace spikes caused by per-kernel slab allocations and eager KV materialization during batched replay. This PR implements two complementary runtime optimizations to reduce peak transient GPU footprint: 1) an ephemeral stride allocator (ESSA) that allocates small, stride-aligned staging lanes per-kernel invocation and reclaims them deterministically at kernel boundary to minimize fragmentation; 2) KV lazy materialization that defers allocation and device-copy of KV tensors until first-touch in the decode loop and allows lightweight shadow entries for routing and prefetch. Design highlights: ESSA uses a compact freelist of fixed-size strides with kernel-aware padding and optional coalescing for consecutive small requests; it supports CUDA stream ownership semantics and a fast-path for single-request kernels. KV lazy materialization introduces a two-state entry (shadow/present) where shadow entries carry metadata and a small CPU-side token; the scheduler can prefetch hotset entries based on recent access windows. The batching scheduler was adapted to prefer low-workspace kernel variants when mixing sequence lengths and to provide a prefetch budget so that KV prefetches don't oversubscribe ESSA. Results: synthetic long-context chat benchmark (max_seq=64k, steady-state) shows median peak transient GPU workspace reduced by 18-28% across A100/RTX6000 profiles; 95th percentile latency improved 5-12% under tight SLOs due to fewer out-of-memory stalls; early customer internal test on a reranking workload saw 22% lower p95 memory headroom. Backwards compatibility and flags: changes are guarded behind runtime flags --enable-ephemeral-scratch and --kv-lazy-materialize. There are no changes to public SDK APIs. Checklist: [x] design doc and microbenchmarks added, [x] unit + integration tests for allocator/race-scenarios, [x] perf bench harness and regression guard, [x] telemetry counters for stride waste and lazy hits. Risk & mitigation: potential race on stream synchronization was mitigated by adding explicit cudaEvent handoff in the ESSA ownership transfer path and a stress test in multi-stream mode. Rollback: runtime flag disables both features, and revert PR is trivial if needed. Related: builds on ENG-7432 (scratch fragmentation incident post-2024-12) and pairs with ENG-7491 (kv hotset profiling).
